t: Minimum Cost to Make Array Equalindromic
o: Cost to convert all elements to a common y is Σ|nums[i]-y|, minimized at the median — but y must be palindromic. So: sort, take the median, and examine the nearest palindromes around it. There are fewer than 20,000 palindromes below 1e9 (built from halves 1..99999), so generating them all and binary-searching around the median is cheap. Example [10,12,13,14,15]: median 13, nearest palindrome 11 gives cost 11.
k: Absolute-deviation cost is minimized at the median, so only palindromes near the median matter.
Palindromes < 1e9 are generated from a mirrored half; there are ~20k of them.

a.i: Generate every palindrome < 1e9 by mirroring halves (both odd and even lengths), sort them, locate the median of nums via binary search, and evaluate cost for a handful of neighboring palindromes. The true optimum is the closest palindrome on either side of the median since cost is piecewise-linear and convex in y.
s: Generate all palindromes < 1e9 from halves 1..99999 and sort them.
Binary-search the insertion point of m among palindromes.
Evaluate Σ|x-p| for a few palindromes around that point; return the minimum.
a.t: O(P log P + n log n) with P ≈ 20000 palindromes; cost evaluations are O(n) each over a constant window.
a.sp: O(P + n) for the palindrome list and sorted copy.

w: Key pitfalls: palindromes must be < 1e9 (values up to 1e9-1 fit), use 64-bit costs, and check a couple of candidates on each side of the median rather than exactly one. Follow-up: if only nearest-palindrome-to-median were needed, you'd construct candidates by tweaking the median's digits instead of enumerating.
